name: Titans
subhead: 2026 training camp edition — a historic 3-14 meltdown triggers a massive overhaul, Robert Saleh takes over, and Cam Ward's development is everything.

left.title: Front Office & Leadership
items: Complete regime reset. Tennessee's 3-14 collapse in 2025 led to the mid-season firing of Brian Callahan and a complete overhaul, with Robert Saleh installed as the new head coach to salvage Cam Ward's career.

Go-all-in mentality. The Titans spent over $300M in free agency, adding more than 20 veteran players to reset the roster in a single offseason — an aggressive strategy that signals desperation and commitment.
Saleh's reputation on the line. Hired from his defensive coordinator role with San Francisco, Saleh must engineer a turnaround in Year 1 or face questions about his ability to lead.
Camp timeline: Rookies report July 23, veterans July 28.

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: SignedWan'Dale Robinson, WR — four-year, $78M deal for a proven pass-catcher to support Ward.
TradeJermaine Johnson II, EDGE acquired from New York Jets to anchor the pass rush.
SignedFranklin-Myers, EDGE, Solomon Thomas, DT (trade), Taylor, CB, Flott, CB, and Daniel Bellinger, TE — veterans across the depth chart.
DraftedSupporting Ward's development: WR Carnell Tate, DE Keldric Faulk in first two rounds to surround the quarterback with playmakers.

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: Cam Ward, QB. The focal point of every move this offseason. His development in Saleh's system, with real pass catchers and pass protection, will determine whether this rebuild works. This is his make-or-break moment in Year 2.
Wan'Dale Robinson, WR. Signed to be the #1 target and stabilizing presence for a sophomore quarterback who needs reliable options.
Robert Saleh's defense. The former 49ers DC brings a proven defensive philosophy; this unit should be far better than 2025's disaster.
Jermaine Johnson II, EDGE. Acquired to provide immediate pass-rush impact — the Titans need sacks and pressure around Ward.
The youth movement. Carnell Tate and Keldric Faulk were drafted to support Ward long-term, creating a young receiving and defensive core.

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: Tennessee threw everything at the 3-14 problem, spending over $300M to overhaul the roster in a single offseason. Robert Saleh arrives to engineer the turnaround, Cam Ward gets real weapons and protection, and Wan'Dale Robinson becomes his safety blanket. This is a team betting on aggressive veteran addition and coach change to salvage a sophomore quarterback who had every excuse to fail last year. If Saleh and Ward both thrive, this camp will be remembered as the turning point. If not, expect questions about whether this massive bet was the answer to the wrong question.
